title: fix(spec): one voice on an undeclared view key, and one report per record
body:
Fixes #10039

An otherwise valid view container carrying one undeclared key drew two contradicting messages out of `defineStack`:

```
WARN:  defineStack: views.v1.bogusViewKey: 'bogusViewKey' is not a declared view key,
       so its value is dropped at load.
THREW: ✗ views.0: Unrecognized key(s) on this view container: `bogusViewKey`. …
```

The warning promises a silent drop — the view loads, minus one key. The refusal one step later says nothing loads at all. An author who reads the warning and stops there draws the opposite conclusion from the truth.

## Root cause 1 — the lint read posture off a different schema than the parse

`lintUnknownAuthoringKeys` took each collection's unknown-key posture from `getMetadataTypeSchema(type)`. That registry answers a different question: it names the schema for a *persisted metadata body* of that type. What `defineStack` applies to a *stack collection entry* is the element schema in `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`'s own shape — and for `view` the two are not the same object:

| | schema | posture |
| --- | --- | --- |
| type registry | `ViewMetadataSchema` — union over the three persisted runtime shapes | `strip`, 91 keys |
| stack slot | `z.array(ViewSchema)` — the `.strict()` defineView container | `strict`, 15 keys |

`lintUnknownStackKeys` has always avoided exactly this at the top level, and its own source says why: a schema that rejects loudly must make the lint go quiet "rather than become a second, possibly disagreeing voice". The per-collection walker applied the same rule to the wrong schema.

Posture now comes from the stack schema's own slot for the collection.

**Blast radius, measured over all 29 collections `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` names** (script and output in the report on #10039): the registry and the stack slot agree everywhere except

- `views` — `strip`/91 vs `strict`/15 → **leaves the lintable set**;
- `themes`, `analyticsCubes` — unregistered in the type registry, `strict` in the stack schema → skipped either way.

For every collection that still lints, the stack slot's element is the *identical node* the registry returns, so the walk itself is unchanged there. `connectors` is the honest remainder — it genuinely warns and drops.

## Root cause 2 — every finding on a union root was emitted twice

`lintUnknownKeysAgainstSchema` reported the root record itself **and** handed that same record to `descend`, whose object arm skipped `depth === 0` ("already reported by the caller") while its union arm had no such guard. `view` was the only union root in the wild, so `defineStack` never showed it — the module-level warn-once set in `warnUnknownAuthoringKeys` absorbed the second copy — while every other consumer of the exported walker saw both.

The root report now lives in `descend` alone, so each record is reported by exactly one place. The dedupe set stays: it is a warn-once-per-process mechanism with its own purpose (`warnConversionNotice` uses the same shape), and it was masking the defect, not causing it.

That also closes a latent third copy: a discriminated-union root whose branch the author *did* pick was reported once against the merged key set and again against the branch's. It is now reported once, against the branch — the narrower and more accurate set.

## Scope

`Clause-②: no` holds. The parse is untouched and `defineStack` accept/reject behaviour is byte-identical; only which of the two existing voices speaks changes. The strip/strict boundary itself is not moved.

## API change (why the changeset is `minor`, not `patch`)

`lintUnknownAuthoringKeys` and `listLintableAuthoringCollections` now take `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` as a **required** parameter, injected the same way and for the same cycle reason `lintUnknownStackKeys` already required it (`stack.zod.ts` imports this module).

Required rather than optional deliberately: an omitted argument falling back to the type registry would silently reinstate the bug — the silent-loss shape this whole rule family exists to report, and the thing the module's own docblock argues against for the sibling function. Every in-repo call site (`defineStack`, `os validate`, `os compile`) already had the schema in hand for the sibling call on the adjacent line.

The dispatch brief predicted a `patch` changeset. Flagging the deviation rather than absorbing it: the behavioural fix alone is a patch, the signature is not.

## Verification

All of the below at `51b23d26b` (tree `bbebc1c8`), merge base `cc21aad8e`.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` — **414 files / 11044 tests passed**.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec --filter @objectstack/cli run typecheck` — both `Done`; spec's `check:test-typecheck` reports `OK` with its debt ledger unmoved.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run test/metadata-type-schema-gate.test.ts test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` — 2 files / 16 tests passed.
- Gate union re-derived from the **actual** diff with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` (no paths passed) — 25 gates, all green. The re-derivation caught 5 the first pass missed, because the changeset file joined the change set after it: `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`, `check:objectui-changeset`, `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-empty-changeset`. It also named `check:stack-collection-maps`, which the dispatch brief's predicted list did not.

**Reverse verification**, direction declared before running: reverting *only* the duplicate-emission half must make union roots report twice while object roots stay at one.

| probe | fix reverted | fix in place |
| --- | --- | --- |
| plain union root | `2` — `probe.zzz`, `probe.zzz` | `1` — `probe.zzz` |
| discriminated union, branch picked | `3` — `probe.zzz`, `probe.b`, `probe.zzz` | `2` — `probe.b`, `probe.zzz` |
| plain object root (control) | `1` | `1` |
| nested strip object (control) | `1` | `1` |

Observed as predicted. The mutation was confirmed on disk by grepping for the reintroduced text before running (`1` hit each for the caller-side report and the `if (depth > 0)` guard), and the restore leg was confirmed `0`/`0` plus byte-identical to the pre-mutation file. No build or `dist/` is involved — the probe imports `packages/spec/src/**` directly through `tsx`, so there is no stale-artifact path for a false green to hide in.

The "before" side of the posture fix is not an ablation but a direct measurement on unmodified `origin/main`: `lintables` advertised `[connectors, views]` and the repro produced `findings: 2` alongside the throw. After: `lintables` is `[connectors]` and the repro produces `findings: 0` for the view key, with the strict-container refusal as the only voice.

## Tests

- `reads posture from the schema the PARSE applies, not the type registry (#10039)` — asserts `view` is out of the lintable set **and** that running the walk explicitly against the registry schema still reproduces the old contradicting finding, so the exclusion cannot quietly become true for an unrelated reason later.
- `lets the strict container refusal be the only voice on an undeclared view key` — the card's fixture verbatim; both halves (lint silent, parse refuses and still names the key), because silence alone would also be produced by a walker that broke.
- `warns exactly once through defineStack, without the warn-once set doing the work` — asserts the finding list itself (what every non-`defineStack` consumer sees) and then the console door, on a key unique to the test so the module-level warn-once set cannot make it pass vacuously.
- `reports a union root once — the merged set, or the branch the author picked` — the duplication mechanism, pinned on injected schemas plus two unchanged controls. This is where the union-walk coverage that used to ride on the live `view` collection now lives; the nested-descent block points at it.
- The cross-collection walk assertion no longer runs through `new Set(...)`. That dedupe was a mask over this defect sitting inside the test that would otherwise have caught it.
